speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me today. You've presented with gait and limb ataxia along with a significant medical history; to begin narrowing down the cause, have you noticed any recent changes in your memory, personality, or vision?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. To help me determine if this is due to a spinal or brainstem issue, have you noticed any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your limbs, and have you experienced any falls?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that; a history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab is a significant risk factor for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), which can cause gait ataxia. Have you noticed any recent worsening of vision, such as blurriness, or any new difficulties speaking? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain - Findings: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). Comments: T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Patient
text: The walking difficulty and coordination problems are the main issues. I do not have chest pain or other major symptoms besides the neurological problems. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.
